issues.legal_issue: A conviction for brothel management or a prostitution-related offence permits an eviction order even when the premises are outside the specified sensitive area.
material_facts: The occupiers were convicted of managing a brothel and knowingly permitting prostitutes to use a public place for their trade.
The premises were outside the specified distance from the public institutions covered by the distance-based restriction.
Following the convictions, the court ordered the occupiers evicted, and the appeal challenged that order.
issues.conclusion: A court may order eviction following a conviction for an offence under section 3 or section 7, whether or not the premises are within the specified distance of a sensitive public place. The appeal was dismissed and the eviction order upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 18(1) and 18(2) of the Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act, 1956, the distance limitation in section 18(1) does not restrict eviction orders made after conviction under section 3 or section 7. Section 18(2) imports the eviction orders in section 18(1), not all the conditions governing the separate procedure in that subsection. Section 3(3) makes the lease void upon conviction for keeping a brothel, supporting eviction of the occupier. Section 7(2)(a) does not require the public place to be within the specified distance, and section 18(2) applies to convictions under section 7, including under that paragraph. The Court distinguished the separate classes addressed by sections 18(1) and 18(2), relying on Sub-Divisional Magistrate v. Ram Kali, and interpreted the ambiguous provision purposively to advance its remedy and suppress the mischief, applying Heydon’s Case.

predicates.eviction_order_appeal_after_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an eviction order made after a criminal conviction.
predicates.conviction_for_brothel_or_prostitution_o: The occupier was convicted of managing a brothel or of a prostitution-related offence.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an eviction order made after a conviction for managing a brothel or a prostitution-related offence, the court may order the occupier's eviction.
